extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, classical scholars, and historians of mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and authorial decisions for composing a scholarly history of Greek mathematics, including choices of arrangement, scope, classification, and level of technical detail suitable for both mathematicians and classical scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement (subject-based vs chronological)
rubrics_metrics.description: In this book I have adopted a new arrangement, mainly according to subjects, the nature of which and the reasons for which will be made clear by an illustration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heath argues for organizing material mainly by subject rather than strictly chronologically; this helps to collect related developments (e.g. all solutions of a famous problem) so relations and identities between them become clearer. The subject-based plan may cause repetition and require cross-references but yields greater unity and comprehensibility for thematic developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group all recorded solutions of a famous problem together
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the case of a famous problem ... Under a chronological arrangement this problem comes up afresh on the occasion of each new solution. Now it is obvious that, if all the recorded solutions are collected together, it is much easier to see the relations, amounting in some cases to substantial identity, between them, and to get a comprehensive view of the history of the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For special problems (doubling the cube, squaring the circle, trisecting an angle) collect and present all recorded solutions in a single section to show their interrelations and provide a comprehensive treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate chapters for major personalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The outstanding personalities of Euclid and Archimedes demand chapters to themselves. ... The imperishable and unique monuments of the genius of these two men must be detached from their surroundings and seen as a whole if we would appreciate to the full the pre-eminent place which they occupy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the work of major figures in dedicated chapters to present their contributions as coherent wholes, allowing readers to appreciate their full significance and style apart from broader chronological narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show course of argument and methods in significant cases
rubrics_metrics.description: I have therefore taken pains, in the most significant cases, to show the course of the argument in sufficient detail to enable a competent mathematician to grasp the method used and to apply it, if he will, to other similar investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not limit the history to summaries of results; where significant, reproduce or explain proofs and procedures in enough detail for a competent mathematician to understand and, if desired, reuse the methods. Emphasize procedure as well as conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate new texts and recent scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: At the date when he wrote, however, Dr. Gow had necessarily to rely upon the works of the pioneers ... Since then the subject has been very greatly advanced; new texts have been published, important new documents have been discovered, and researches by scholars and mathematicians in different countries have thrown light on many obscure points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A modern history must take account of newly published texts, discovered documents, and recent research; relying solely on earlier pioneer works can leave accounts outdated in detail and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept repetition and cross-references to secure unity
rubrics_metrics.description: The arrangement which I have adopted necessitates (as does any other order of exposition) a certain amount of repetition and cross-references; but only in this way can the necessary unity be given to the whole narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When organizing by topic rather than chronology, be prepared to repeat material and include cross-references: this is an acceptable trade-off to produce a coherent, unified presentation of themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify mathematics into clear branches for organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaning and classification of mathematics ... (a) Arithmetic and logistic ... (b) Geometry and geodaesia ... (c) Physical subjects, mechanics, optics, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an explicit classification scheme (arithmetic/logistic; geometry/geodaesia; physical/applied subjects) to structure the account and clarify the boundaries and interrelations of different mathematical activities in the Greek world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize Greek foundations, methods, and terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: For the mathematician the important consideration is that the foundations of mathematics and a great portion of its content are Greek. The Greeks laid down the first principles, invented the methods ab initio, and fixed the terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing for mathematicians, stress the foundational role of Greek mathematics — origins of principles, methods, and terminology — to show continuity between ancient contributions and later mathematical development.
